a1-unit-16.16.1 Toms animal quiz:
Tom: Hi, Kate! I have an animal quiz for my students tomorrow. Can I try it with you?
Kate: Sure! But I'm busy, so be quick!
Tom: OK. Question one. Which animals are faster: camels or elephants?
Kate: Hmm… Elephants are bigger, but camels are faster, I think.
Tom: Correct! Camels can run at forty miles per hour. Elephants run at fifteen.
Kate: Ha! That's easy.
Tom: Question two. Which animals are heavier: lions or tigers?
Kate: Lions! They're the kings!
Tom: No, sorry. Tigers are heavier. A tiger weighs about four hundred and eighty-seven pounds. A lion weighs about four hundred.
Kate: Oh, really?
Tom: Question three. Which animals are more dangerous to people: sharks or snakes?
Kate: Sharks, of course! I watch the movies!
Tom: No! Snakes are more dangerous. Sharks kill about six people every year. Snakes kill about one hundred thousand!
Kate: One hundred thousand? Wow!
Tom: Last question. Which animals are more intelligent: chimps or dolphins?
Kate: Chimps. They're more like us.
Tom: Well, it's difficult to say. But dolphins have a better memory than chimps.
Kate: So I have one point. You're a terrible quiz master, Tom!
Tom: Ha! And you're a worse player than my students!

a1-unit-17.17.1 Travel podcast:
Host: Hi, everyone! Welcome to Travel Talk. Today I'm here with Paulo, a travel photographer from Brazil. Hi, Paulo!
Paulo: Hi! Thanks for having me.
Host: Let's start with an easy question. What's the easiest country to visit?
Paulo: I think New Zealand. People speak English, and they're very friendly. It's one of the safest countries in the world. But it's the farthest country from my home. It's more than twenty hours by plane!
Host: And what's the most expensive country?
Paulo: Switzerland! A cheap lunch is twenty-five dollars, and a hotel is three hundred and fifty dollars a night. But it's one of the prettiest countries in the world. The mountains are amazing.
Host: What's the smallest country you know?
Paulo: The Vatican, in Rome. It's the smallest country in the world. Only about eight hundred people live there.
Host: And the hottest place?
Paulo: Death Valley, in California. In summer, it's more than fifty degrees Celsius. Take a lot of water!
Host: Wow! And finally, what's the best place in the world?
Paulo: That's easy. My home, São Paulo! It has the best food in the world!
Host: Ha! Thanks, Paulo!

a1-unit-19.19.1 Summer and winter a video call:
Tom: Hi, Ana! What are you doing?
Ana: Hi, Tom! I'm sitting in my garden, and I'm having a cold juice. It's very hot today!
Tom: Really? What's the temperature?
Ana: It's thirty-two degrees. That's about ninety in Fahrenheit. The sun is shining and the sky is blue.
Tom: Wow! Here in Chicago, it's snowing! Look out of the window.
Ana: Oh, it's beautiful! Are people walking in the snow?
Tom: Yes, they are. People are wearing big coats and hats. And the wind is blowing. It's minus five degrees. That's about twenty-three in Fahrenheit.
Ana: Brr! What are you wearing?
Tom: I'm wearing two sweaters! And I'm drinking hot chocolate.
Ana: Ha! It's summer here in December. Leo and Marcos are swimming in the pool right now.
Tom: Lucky you! Is it always hot in São Paulo in December?
Ana: Usually, yes. But it often rains in the afternoon. Look, the sky is getting dark… Oh no, it's starting to rain!
Tom: Ha! Now we're both inside!

a1-unit-20.20.1 A beach vacation:
Tom: Hi, Ana! Where are you? I can hear the ocean!
Ana: Hi, Tom! I'm on vacation in Bahia with my family. I'm at the beach.
Tom: Lucky you! What are you doing right now?
Ana: I'm sunbathing and talking to you!
Tom: Ha! Where's Marcos?
Ana: He's swimming in the ocean. He swims every morning on vacation.
Tom: And what's Leo doing?
Ana: He's eating ice cream. Chocolate, of course! He loves chocolate.
Tom: Is Paulo there too?
Ana: Yes, he is. He's in the city. He's taking photos of the old streets and buildings in Salvador. He takes a lot of photos. It's his job!
Tom: And your parents? What are they doing?
Ana: They're buying souvenirs at the market.
Tom: Why are they buying souvenirs?
Ana: So they can give them to their friends.
Tom: That's nice. Well, I'm working today, and it's snowing again!
Ana: Oh, poor Tom! Hey, Leo's ice cream looks delicious. Now I want ice cream too!
